families.title: The Kollár–Pardon universal-cover conjecture
families.description: Proves the Kollár–Pardon conjecture: the semialgebraic universal covers of connected normal projective complex varieties are exactly products D×C^m×F, with D bounded symmetric and F simply connected, normal, and projective. A universal cover is quasi-projective exactly when the bounded symmetric factor is absent. In particular, a smooth projective variety covered by C^n has a finite étale cover by an abelian variety.

families.title: Counterexamples to Zariski's multiplicity conjecture
families.description: Disproves Zariski's multiplicity conjecture by constructing reduced holomorphic hypersurface germs that are ambiently homeomorphic but have different multiplicities. The examples include hypersurfaces in C^4 with isolated critical points and multiplicities four and five.

families.title: The Global Spherical Shell conjecture
families.description: Every connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII with b_2>0 contains a global spherical shell, proving the positive-b_2 Global Spherical Shell conjecture. Such a shell is a holomorphically embedded neighborhood of the standard three-sphere in C^2\0\ whose complement is connected.

manuscripts.short_title: Global Spherical Shells on Minimal Surfaces of Class VII
manuscripts.title: Global Spherical Shells on Minimal Surfaces of Class VII

families.title: The LeBrun–Salamon conjecture and projective contact classification
families.description: Proves the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture: every closed connected positive quaternionic-Kähler manifold of real dimension at least eight is homothetic to a compact symmetric Wolf space. It also proves contact-Fano homogeneity and classifies smooth connected complex projective contact manifolds of complex dimension at least three: those with b_2=1 are adjoint varieties with their canonical contact structures, while those with b_2≥2 have underlying manifold P(T^*Z) for a smooth projective variety Z.

manuscripts.short_title: Contact Fano manifolds and the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture
manuscripts.title: Contact Fano manifolds and the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture

families.title: The generalized Mukai conjecture
families.description: Proves the generalized Mukai conjecture: every positive-dimensional smooth complex projective Fano manifold of dimension n, Picard number ρ and pseudoindex satisfies ρ(-1)≤n, with equality exactly for (P^-1)^ρ. Here the pseudoindex is the least anticanonical degree of a rational curve.

families.title: The μ-constant problem for surface singularities
families.description: Proves topo log ical right-triviality for every holomorphic one-parameter family of isolated hypersurface singularities in C^3 with constant Milnor number, resolving the surface case of the μ-constant problem. After shrinking the parameter disk and representatives, ambient homeomorphisms vary jointly continuously, fix the origin section and preserve the defining functions.

manuscripts.short_title: Topo log ical triviality of mu-constant families of surface singularities
manuscripts.title: Topo log ical triviality of mu-constant families of surface singularities

families.title: Virasoro constraints for complete intersections and projective bundles
families.description: Proves the full ordinary unreduced descendant Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections in complex projective space, in every genus and curve class with arbitrary cohomo log y insertions. The constraints also pass from any smooth projective complex base satisfying them to the projectivization of every algebraic vector bundle of rank at least two, and hence to projective-bundle towers.

manuscripts.short_title: Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections
manuscripts.title: Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections

families.title: Bounded klt complements for Fano contractions
families.description: Proves the finite-rational-coefficient form of Shokurov’s bounded-klt-complement conjecture for ε-lc complex Fano-type pairs with nef anti-log-canonical divisor. For ε-lc Fano contractions over any algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, it gives klt complements near every base point, with index bounded only by dimension and positive rational ε.

families.title: The Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six
families.description: Proves the Campana–Peternell conjecture in complex dimension six: every smooth connected complex projective Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous.

manuscripts.short_title: The Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six
manuscripts.title: The Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six

families.title: Anticanonical nonvanishing under smooth semipositivity
families.description: If X is a smooth connected complex projective variety and -K_X admits a smooth Hermitian metric with nonnegative curvature, then H^0(X,-mK_X)≠0 for some m>0. Thus smooth semipositivity forces a nonzero section of a positive tensor power of the anticanonical bundle in every dimension.

manuscripts.short_title: Exact orders and invariant linear systems
manuscripts.title: Exact orders and invariant linear systems

families.title: Quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level
families.description: Proves the unramified de Rham quantum geometric Langlands equivalence for every connected simple complex algebraic group on every smooth projective connected complex curve, at every shifted level cCQ. It identifies the full derived categories of twisted D-modules for the group and its Langlands dual, retaining all global forms and connected components.

manuscripts.short_title: Global quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level
manuscripts.title: Global quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level

families.title: Koebe's circle-domain conjecture and circle-domain rigidity
families.description: Resolves the existence part of Koebe's circle-domain conjecture: every domain in the Riemann sphere is conformally equivalent to a domain whose complementary components are round disks or points. It also proves that circle domains with conformally removable boundary are rigid, meaning every conformal equivalence to another circle domain is Möbius, establishing this direction of the He–Schramm conjecture.

families.title: Brennan's conjecture and a counterexample to Kraetzer's prediction
families.description: Proves Brennan's conjecture: for every conformal bijection φ from a simply connected plane domain onto the disk, |φ'|^s is area-integrable for 4/3<s<4. The sharp universal integral-means identity is B_S(t)=|t|-1 for t≤-2. A strict bound B_b(-1)<1/4 for bounded univalent functions disproves Kraetzer's prediction at that parameter.

families.title: The Falconer distance conjecture
families.description: Resolves the Falconer distance conjecture in every dimension d≥2: every compact set ER^d with Hausdorff dimension greater than d/2 determines a set of Euclidean distances of positive Lebesgue measure.

manuscripts.short_title: The Falconer distance conjecture in all dimensions
manuscripts.title: The Falconer distance conjecture in all dimensions

families.title: Kakeya in three and four dimensions
families.description: Resolves the Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions and the Hausdorff-dimension conjecture in four. In three dimensions, the radius-δ tube maximal operator maps L^3(R^3) to L^3(S^2) with norm O_(δ^-) for every >0. In four dimensions, every set containing a unit segment in every direction has Hausdorff dimension four.

families.title: The L log L Fourier-convergence conjecture
families.description: Proves that the ordinary symmetric Fourier partial sums of every complex-valued function in L log L(T) converge almost everywhere along the full sequence. This resolves the classical sufficiency conjecture at the L log L scale.

manuscripts.short_title: Almost-everywhere Fourier convergence in L log L
manuscripts.title: Almost-everywhere Fourier convergence in L log L

families.title: Ultraflat real Littlewood polynomials
families.description: Constructs polynomials with N consecutive coefficients in \-1,1\ whose modulus is (1+o(1))√N uniformly on the entire unit circle, for every sufficiently large integer length N. Thus real Littlewood polynomials are ultraflat, including at the real endpoints. Their binary merit factors tend to infinity, disproving Turyn's bounded-merit-factor conjecture.

manuscripts.short_title: Nearly minimal maxima and positive minima of Littlewood polynomials
manuscripts.title: Nearly minimal maxima and positive minima of Littlewood polynomials

manuscripts.short_title: Asymptotically minimal maxima of real Littlewood polynomials
manuscripts.title: Asymptotically minimal maxima of real Littlewood polynomials

families.title: Fourier restriction for positively curved surfaces
families.description: Proves the diagonal Fourier extension conjecture for positively curved surfaces in three dimensions. For every compact smooth positively curved surface ΣR^3, including surfaces with boundary, the extension operator is bounded from L^p(Σ) to L^p(R^3) for every p>3.

families.title: The three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture
families.description: Resolves the three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture in its strict range: the Bochner–Riesz multipliers of order δ are bounded on L^p(R^3) for every 1≤p≤∞ whenever δ>\3|1/p-1/2|-1/2,0\.

families.title: Sogge's local smoothing conjecture in dimension three
families.description: Resolves Sogge's local smoothing conjecture for the Euclidean wave equation in three spatial dimensions. The estimate holds throughout the full strict range 2<p<∞, with Sobolev regularity above \0,1-3/p\. In particular, the critical L^3 estimate holds with every positive Sobolev loss.

manuscripts.short_title: Critical local smoothing for the three-dimensional wave equation
manuscripts.title: Critical local smoothing for the three-dimensional wave equation

families.title: The Sobolev endpoint in Carleson's Schrödinger convergence problem
families.description: Proves almost-everywhere convergence e^itΔff as t0 for every fH^n/(2(n+1))(R^n) and every dimension n≥2. This attains the sharp Sobolev equality case of Carleson's Schrödinger convergence problem, including the planar endpoint H^1/3.

families.title: The David–Semmes Riesz-transform problem in higher codimension
families.description: Resolves the remaining higher-codimension Riesz-transform rectifiability problem: for d≥4 and 2≤n≤d-2, an n-Ahlfors–David regular Radon measure on R^d is uniformly n-rectifiable whenever its n-dimensional Riesz transform is uniformly L^2-bounded over all positive hard truncations. The rectifiability bounds depend only on dimension, regularity and operator bounds.

manuscripts.short_title: Riesz transforms and uniform rectifiability in higher codimension
manuscripts.title: Riesz transforms and uniform rectifiability in higher codimension

families.title: Maximal and variational bounds for the triangular Hilbert transform
families.description: Proves maximal and annular r-variation bounds, for every r>2, from complex L^3(R^2)×L^3(R^2) to L^3/2(R^2). The maximal estimate controls both hard truncation endpoints and gives almost-everywhere and norm convergence. Pairing with a third input settles the triangular Hilbert transform estimate at the symmetric L^3×L^3×L^3 point.

manuscripts.short_title: Annular variation of the triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point
manuscripts.title: Annular variation of the triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point

manuscripts.short_title: An L^3 bound for the dyadic triangular Hilbert form
manuscripts.title: An L^3 bound for the dyadic triangular Hilbert form

manuscripts.short_title: The maximal triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point
manuscripts.title: The maximal triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point

families.title: Stein's conjecture for Hilbert transforms along Lipschitz directions
families.description: Proves a uniform strong L^2 bound for the planar Hilbert transform along any Lipschitz unit vector field, at integration lengths bounded by an absolute multiple of its reciprocal Lipschitz constant. The estimate is uniform over inner truncations and yields an L^2-bounded principal-value operator, establishing Stein's weak-type conjecture at this short scale.

manuscripts.short_title: A uniform Hilbert transform estimate for Lipschitz directions
manuscripts.title: A uniform Hilbert transform estimate for Lipschitz directions

families.title: The geometric case of the Erdos similarity conjecture
families.description: For every fixed q(0,1), constructs compact subsets of [0,1] with measure arbitrarily close to one containing no translated and nontrivially dilated copy of \q^n:n≥1\, with dilations of either sign. This resolves the geometric-progression case of the Erdos similarity conjecture for every ratio.

manuscripts.short_title: The geometric case of the Erdos similarity conjecture
manuscripts.title: The geometric case of the Erdos similarity conjecture

manuscripts.short_title: The dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture
manuscripts.title: The dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture

families.title: Endpoint regularity of the planar centered maximal function
families.description: Resolves the planar centered-disk case of the Hajasz–Onninen maximal-function regularity problem. For every real fW^1,1(R^2), the centered disk maximal function satisfies \|Mf\|_1≤C\|f\|_1 with an absolute constant. It belongs locally to W^1,1 and has a globally integrable weak gradient.

manuscripts.short_title: An Endpoint Gradient Bound for the Centered Disk Maximal Operator
manuscripts.title: An Endpoint Gradient Bound for the Centered Disk Maximal Operator

families.title: An L^3 bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform
families.description: Proves that the principal-value trilinear Hilbert transform with shifts x-t, x-2t, x-3t is bounded from L^3(R)^3 to L^1(R). This resolves the L^3 exponent case of the standard conjecture for slopes 1,2,3.

manuscripts.short_title: An L^3 bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform
manuscripts.title: An L^3 bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform

families.title: The Mahler conjectures and symplectic width
families.description: Resolves the symmetric and nonsymmetric geometric Mahler conjectures in every dimension, with Hanner polytopes and simplices as the respective volume-product minimizers and all equality cases classified. The corresponding sharp functional Mahler inequalities also hold. For n≥2, every symmetric polar product K×K^ in dimension 2n has Gromov width 4.

families.title: Petty's projection-volume conjecture and simplex counterexamples
families.description: Proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture in the remaining dimensions n≥4: ellipsoids uniquely minimize projection-body volume at fixed body volume. Also establishes the full Lutwak–Petty projection inequalities. In contrast, products of simplices exceed Brannen's proposed simplex maximum for normalized projection-body volume by an exponential factor in every sufficiently large dimension.

families.title: Bounded-distortion L_1 embeddings of planar and bounded-treewidth graphs
families.description: Resolves the planar and bounded-treewidth cases of the Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair conjecture. Shortest-path metrics of finite connected graphs with arbitrary positive edge lengths embed into real L_1 with universal distortion for planar graphs, and distortion depending only on treewidth for bounded-treewidth graphs. The corresponding multicommodity flow–cut gaps are uniformly bounded.

families.title: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice
families.description: Proves that the triangular lattice minimizes the lower limit of energy per particle for every nonnegative completely monotone potential of squared distance among locally finite planar configurations of centered-disk density one. It also minimizes unit-background renormalized Riesz energies for 0<s<2 and Coulomb energy, resolving Sandier–Serfaty and the two-dimensional Brauchart–Hardin–Saff conjecture on the linear term of optimal spherical logarithmic energy.

families.title: The logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture
families.description: Proves the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality for origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension, and the scalar-dilation B-conjecture for all even log-concave Radon measures. For Lebesgue volume it also proves the additive L_p Brunn–Minkowski inequality for full-dimensional origin-symmetric convex bodies throughout 0<p<1.

families.title: The optimal order of convex-body covering density
families.description: Determines the optimal worst-case covering density as Θ(n log n), for both lattice and unrestricted translative coverings. Every convex body in R^n, n≥2, admits a lattice covering of density at most Cn log n; centrally symmetric examples in every sufficiently large dimension require at least cn log n even without the lattice restriction, for absolute c,C>0.

families.title: Dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for subgaussian log-concave measures
families.description: Proves a dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for centered log-concave densities with uniformly subgaussian linear marginals, with constant bounded by a universal multiple of the squared linear subgaussian parameter.

families.title: Subpolynomial dimension reduction in L_p
families.description: For every fixed 1<p<∞ and distortion D>1, every n-point subset of real L_p embeds into ℓ_p^d with distortion at most D and dimension d=n^o(1), answering Naor's sublinear-dimension question for p≠2. In contrast, exact embeddings require worst-case dimension Θ(n^2) when p≠2.

families.title: Hyperbolicity cones without semidefinite lifts
families.description: Disproves the Projected Lax conjecture: some hyperbolicity cones are not spectrahedral shadows. The examples admit no exact finite affine semidefinite lift, regardless of the number of auxiliary variables or the real coefficients used. This also disproves the generalized Lax conjecture that every hyperbolicity cone is spectrahedral.

manuscripts.short_title: An Exact Semidefinite Lift of a Nonspectrahedral Hyperbolicity Cone
manuscripts.title: An Exact Semidefinite Lift of a Nonspectrahedral Hyperbolicity Cone

families.title: The Gaussian propeller conjecture
families.description: Proves that the sum of squared Gaussian first moments of any finite measurable partition is at most 9/(8π). In dimension at least two, three planar sectors of angle 2π/3, extended orthogonally, attain the bound. Combined with the separate Unique Games theorem, this proves NP-hardness of improving the loss factor (8π/9)(1-1/k) for identity-target kernel clustering with fixed k≥3 on rational centered positive semidefinite inputs.

manuscripts.short_title: The Gaussian propeller bound in every dimension
manuscripts.title: The Gaussian propeller bound in every dimension

families.title: The Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström conjecture
families.description: Proves that any finite sequence in the Euclidean unit ball of R^d admits signs keeping every partial sum within C√d, independently of length. Consequently every zero-sum family can be reordered with the same bound on unsigned partial sums. A matching lower bound gives the optimal order S_2(d)=Θ(√d).

families.title: A negative answer to the Lang–Plaut problem
families.description: Every infinite-dimensional real Banach space contains a compact doubling set that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional normed space. The doubling constant is universal. This answers the Lang–Plaut problem negatively, even for compact subsets of Hilbert space.

manuscripts.short_title: A doubling Hilbert subset with no finite-dimensional bi-Lipschitz embedding
manuscripts.title: A doubling Hilbert subset with no finite-dimensional bi-Lipschitz embedding

families.title: The sharp distortion of edit distance into ℓ_1
families.description: Determines the least distortion of embedding edit distance on words of length at most d into real ℓ_1: it is (Θ(√logd\,log log d)). Insertions, deletions and substitutions have unit cost. The constants are uniform over all finite alphabets with at least two symbols, even when the alphabet grows with d; binary words already force the lower bound.

families.title: A counterexample to Bang's cylinder-covering bound
families.description: Covers the entire closed regular tetrahedron by finitely many cylinders with compact triangular perpendicular bases whose total area is less than half its smallest orthogonal projection area. This disproves Bang's half-area cylinder-covering bound and the stronger directionwise normalized conjecture in dimension three.

families.title: The sharp simplex conjecture for isotropic constants
families.description: Proves that simplices uniquely maximize the isotropic constant among convex bodies in every dimension, resolving the strong isotropic constant conjecture. Also establishes the sharp entropy lower bound for log-concave probability densities, with equality precisely for invertible affine images of products of one-sided exponential laws.

manuscripts.short_title: A sharp entropy bound and the simplex inequality for isotropic constants
manuscripts.title: A sharp entropy bound and the simplex inequality for isotropic constants

families.title: The Unique Games Conjecture and optimal approximation thresholds
families.description: Proves Khot's Unique Games Conjecture. Independent direct reductions also establish NP-hardness, on unweighted graphs, of approximation beyond the Goemans–Williamson ratio for Max-Cut, below factor two for Vertex Cover, and within any fixed constant factor for Min-UnCut and directed feedback vertex set. These direct proofs use established PCP and Label Cover hardness results.

families.title: Derandomization of logarithmic space: L=RL=BPL
families.description: Proves L=RL=BPL, resolving derandomization for bounded-error logarithmic-space computation. An effective compiler converts each randomized polynomial-time logarithmic-space machine deciding a language with one-sided or two-sided error into a deterministic logarithmic-space decider with explicit polynomial running-time bounds.

manuscripts.short_title: Exact derandomization of logarithmic space: L = RL = BPL
manuscripts.title: Exact derandomization of logarithmic space: L = RL = BPL

families.title: Quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games
families.description: Gives deterministic algorithms using 2^O((log(L+2))^2) bit operations, for complete binary input length L, for ordinary mean-payoff games and two separate extensions. They compute exact values and optimal positional strategies in ordinary games, the nonnegative expectation-of-liminf value set in turn-based stochastic games, and the winning set for nonnegative liminf mean payoff conjoined with parity. Signed rewards, rational chance probabilities, and parity priorities are unrestricted and binary-encoded.

manuscripts.short_title: Turn-Based Stochastic Mean-Payoff Games in Deterministic Quasipolynomial Time
manuscripts.title: Turn-Based Stochastic Mean-Payoff Games in Deterministic Quasipolynomial Time

manuscripts.short_title: Mean-payoff parity games in quasipolynomial time
manuscripts.title: Mean-payoff parity games in quasipolynomial time

families.title: The 2-to-1 Games Conjecture with perfect completeness
families.description: Proves Khot's 2-to-1 Games Conjecture with perfect completeness: for every fixed rational δ(0,1), it is NP-hard to distinguish satisfiable games from games whose optimum is at most δ, on explicit unweighted instances. The alphabet depends only on δ, and every right-hand label has exactly two preimages under each constraint map.

families.title: Hardness of coloring three-colorable graphs
families.description: It is NP-hard to color a three-colorable graph using any fixed number c≥3 of colors. More strongly, for every fixed 0<δ<1/3, a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT produces simple unweighted graphs that are three-colorable in the satisfiable case and have no independent set of size δn otherwise, where n is the number of vertices.

manuscripts.short_title: Hardness of finding large independent sets in three-colorable graphs
manuscripts.title: Hardness of finding large independent sets in three-colorable graphs

families.title: Matrix multiplication with exponent at most 9/4
families.description: Proves ω≤9/4 over C, giving O_(n^9/4+) arithmetic operations for square matrix multiplication. In characteristic zero, some inner dimension n^a with a>0.465 permits n^2+o(1) rectangular multiplication. Further square bounds give ω<2.258 outside finitely many positive characteristics and ω<2.371054886006746 over every fixed field.

families.title: A cubic permanent–determinant lower bound
families.description: Proves an Ω(n^3) lower bound for the border determinantal complexity of the n×n permanent over C. Even coefficientwise limits of determinants of affine-linear matrices require matrix size at least cn^3, for an absolute c>0 and all sufficiently large n; the same bound therefore holds for exact representations.

manuscripts.short_title: A cubic lower bound for border determinantal complexity of the permanent
manuscripts.title: A cubic lower bound for border determinantal complexity of the permanent

families.title: Integer multiplication below n log n
families.description: Multiplies two n-bit integers exactly at every input length in deterministic worst-case time O(n(logn)^1-κ), with κ=2^-182, on one fixed finite-alphabet Turing machine with finitely many one-dimensional tapes. This disproves the Schönhage–Strassen n log n optimality conjecture in the ordinary multitape bit model.

manuscripts.short_title: Integer multiplication below n log n
manuscripts.title: Integer multiplication below n log n

families.title: Optimal-order randomized k-server on arbitrary metrics
families.description: Establishes a randomized competitive ratio O(log^2(k+1)) for k-server on every metric space, matching the worst-case lower-bound order. One policy serves every finite oblivious request sequence, including on infinite unbounded metrics. On finite rational metrics, a uniform implementation has polynomial preprocessing and per-request bit cost in the input length and log(t+1) at request t, with a finite instance-dependent additive movement constant.

families.title: One-sample matroid prophet inequalities against an almighty adversary
families.description: For every finite matroid known in advance, gives a distribution-independent online rule using one independent sample per element and earning a universal constant fraction of the expected offline optimum. Values are independent and nonnegative, with finite expected optimum. The guarantee holds even when the arrival-order adversary sees all samples, values, and the rule's entire random seed; no polynomial-time implementation is asserted.

manuscripts.short_title: One Sample Suffices for Matroid Prophet Inequalities against an Almighty Adversary
manuscripts.title: One Sample Suffices for Matroid Prophet Inequalities against an Almighty Adversary

families.title: Beyond the square-root exponent for depth-three circuits
families.description: Constructs a single language in deterministic polynomial time whose n-bit membership function requires 2^ω(√n) total gates in unbounded-fan-in OR–AND–OR circuits, at every sufficiently large input length. This crosses the square-root-exponent threshold for explicit depth-three Boolean circuit lower bounds.

manuscripts.short_title: Beyond the Square-Root Exponent for Depth-Three Boolean Circuits
manuscripts.title: Beyond the Square-Root Exponent for Depth-Three Boolean Circuits

families.title: Approximate counting and the perfect-matching entropy conjecture
families.description: Gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting perfect matchings in arbitrary finite simple graphs, with exact detection of zero counts. Also proves the perfect-matching entropy conjecture of Anari, Oveis Gharan, and Vinzant, bounding the maximum entropy of a matching law at every feasible edge-marginal vector in a loopless labelled multigraph, including boundary points.

families.title: Approximate counting of common integer polymatroid bases
families.description: Gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting common integer bases of two integral polymatroids of equal total rank, supplied by exact rank-value oracles. Capacities are binary-encoded, each integer vector counts once, and oracle calls and bit operations outside the oracles are polynomial on every execution. For matroids presented by independence oracles, the results also cover common independent sets of prescribed, unrestricted, or maximum cardinality, even when the ranks differ.

manuscripts.short_title: An FPRAS for Common Integer Polymatroid Bases with Binary Capacities
manuscripts.title: An FPRAS for Common Integer Polymatroid Bases with Binary Capacities

manuscripts.short_title: Approximate counting of common bases of two matroids
manuscripts.title: Approximate counting of common bases of two matroids

families.title: Sampling and counting contingency tables with arbitrary margins
families.description: For nonnegative integer matrices with prescribed row and column sums, gives exact uniform sampling in expected polynomial bit time and almost-uniform sampling in worst-case polynomial bit time. The dimensions and binary-encoded margins are unrestricted. Also gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting such tables with arbitrary individual cell bounds, including structural zeros, with polynomial cost on every execution.

families.title: Uniform identity testing for noncommutative formulas
families.description: For each characteristic, constructs in deterministic polynomial bit time a polynomial-dimensional matrix tuple detecting every nonzero division-free noncommutative formula of bounded size over any field of that characteristic. Rational formulas over Q also admit polynomial-size hitting lists whenever they have a defined rational-matrix evaluation.

manuscripts.short_title: Uniform Matrix Hitting Points in Every Positive Characteristic
manuscripts.title: Uniform Matrix Hitting Points in Every Positive Characteristic

families.title: Uniform sparsest cut: hardness and semidefinite gaps
families.description: Proves that approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut within any fixed constant factor is NP-hard, even with nonnegative rational capacities and unit demands. The Goemans–Linial semidefinite relaxation also has integrality gaps of order at least √logn/(log log n)^3, approaching the square-root-logarithmic upper bound.

families.title: Unbounded bin-packing gaps and the modified integer round-up conjecture
families.description: Disproves the modified integer round-up conjecture of Scheithauer and Terno: the integral bin-packing optimum can exceed its configuration linear-programming value by an arbitrarily large additive constant. Approximating the optimum within any fixed additive constant is also NP-hard, even when every item exceeds 1/6 and each bin holds at most five items.

manuscripts.short_title: Additive hardness and unbounded configuration gaps in bin packing
manuscripts.title: Additive hardness and unbounded configuration gaps in bin packing

families.title: The Courtade–Kumar and Hellinger conjectures
families.description: Proves the Courtade–Kumar conjecture: among Boolean functions of independent uniform bits, a single coordinate retains the most mutual information after independent bit-flip noise. A stronger theorem treats randomized binary summaries at fixed initial information. The Hellinger conjecture is also proved for every Boolean output bias and noise correlation.

families.title: Almost-linear-time exact matching in general graphs
families.description: Gives a randomized algorithm finding an exact maximum-cardinality matching in any simple undirected graph in (n+m)^1+o(1) word time, with success probability at least 2/3. The time bound holds on every computation path. The same guarantees apply to finding a spanning subgraph with prescribed admissible vertex degrees, or deciding that none exists.

manuscripts.short_title: Almost-Linear-Time Maximum-Cardinality Matching in General Graphs
manuscripts.title: Almost-Linear-Time Maximum-Cardinality Matching in General Graphs

families.title: Almost-linear expected-time approximation of edit distance
families.description: For every fixed rational (0,1), gives a randomized (1+) approximation to unit-cost edit distance in worst-case expected time N^1+o(1), with success probability at least 2/3. The strings have total length N and polynomially bounded integer symbols. This is an asymptotic guarantee at fixed accuracy.

manuscripts.short_title: An Almost-Linear Approximation Scheme for Edit Distance
manuscripts.title: An Almost-Linear Approximation Scheme for Edit Distance

families.title: Superpolynomial lower bounds and quasipolynomial reconstruction from deletion traces
families.description: At every fixed deletion probability in (0,1), reconstructing an arbitrary length-n binary string requires n^Ω(log log n) independent traces, ruling out polynomial-sample reconstruction. A uniform decoder achieves quasipolynomial sample and running-time bounds for known fixed rational retention probabilities. When the deletion probability is at most n^- for fixed >0, both bounds become polynomial in the input and parameter encoding.

manuscripts.short_title: A latest-anchor induction with spectrally compact masks for worst-case trace reconstruction
manuscripts.title: A latest-anchor induction with spectrally compact masks for worst-case trace reconstruction

manuscripts.short_title: Quantitative lower bounds for trace reconstruction
manuscripts.title: Quantitative lower bounds for trace reconstruction

families.title: Polynomial-time scheduling on three identical machines
families.description: Resolves the three-processor unit-job scheduling problem of Garey and Johnson: a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm minimizes makespan for nonpreemptive unit-length jobs with arbitrary precedence constraints on three identical parallel machines. For an explicitly given precedence graph, it decides deadline feasibility exactly and constructs a feasible schedule.

manuscripts.short_title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Three-Machine Unit-Job Scheduling
manuscripts.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Three-Machine Unit-Job Scheduling

families.title: The approximation threshold for metric k-median
families.description: Gives a deterministic polynomial-time (1+2/e+)-approximation for finite rational metric k-median with specified candidate facilities, for every fixed >0. Assuming P≠NP, the optimal infimum approximation factor is 1+2/e.

families.title: Exponential semidefinite complexity of perfect matching
families.description: Proves that every exact semidefinite lift of the perfect matching polytope has exponential size, answering Rothvoss's polynomial-size lift question negatively. The bound holds even for the positive semidefinite rank of its odd-cut slack matrix after any fixed shift 0<ρ<1, allowing arbitrary real positive semidefinite factors.

manuscripts.short_title: Exponential PSD rank of positively shifted matching matrices
manuscripts.title: Exponential PSD rank of positively shifted matching matrices

families.title: The asymptotic Gotsman–Linial conjecture
families.description: Proves that a degree-at-most-d polynomial threshold function on the uniform n-dimensional Boolean cube has average sensitivity at most 8d√n, uniformly for 1≤d≤n. Average sensitivity counts expected output changes under single-bit flips. This establishes the asymptotic Gotsman–Linial conjecture, allowing polynomial zeros with sign(0)=1.

manuscripts.short_title: Average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions
manuscripts.title: Average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions

families.title: A factor-two approximation for shortest common superstring
families.description: Gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm constructing a common superstring of length at most twice the optimum for every finite family of explicitly represented strings. The running time is polynomial in the full encoded input length, including symbol labels.

manuscripts.short_title: A Polynomial-Time 2-Approximation for Shortest Common Superstring
manuscripts.title: A Polynomial-Time 2-Approximation for Shortest Common Superstring

families.title: Exponential state costs for two-way automata
families.description: Proves exponential lower bounds both for complementing two-way nondeterministic finite automata and for simulating one-way nondeterministic automata by two-way deterministic ones. The latter resolves the Sakoda–Sipser state-succinctness conjecture over growing finite alphabets; both results rule out polynomial state bounds independent of alphabet size.

families.title: Fourier transforms below n log n
families.description: Gives a deterministic length-n discrete Fourier transform algorithm using O(n(logn)^1-δ) operations for every n, with explicit δ=10^-13. The model uses exact complex arithmetic, unrestricted coefficients and a supplied root of unity, and counts scalar preparation and logarithmic-word indexing.

families.title: Polynomial mixing of graph switches with prescribed degrees
families.description: Resolves the simple-undirected Kannan–Tetali–Vempala conjecture: the lazy edge-switch chain mixes in O(n^8) time for every graphical labeled degree sequence. The same degree-constrained graphs can also be sampled exactly uniformly by an almost-surely terminating algorithm with expected polynomial bit running time.

manuscripts.short_title: Polynomial mixing of the switch chain for every graphical degree sequence
manuscripts.title: Polynomial mixing of the switch chain for every graphical degree sequence

families.title: A counterexample to the quadratic sensitivity conjecture
families.description: Constructs total Boolean functions with block sensitivity bs(f)≥s(f)^α for a fixed α>2, disproving the quadratic strengthening of the Sensitivity Conjecture. Here s(f) counts influential individual-bit flips, while block sensitivity allows disjoint groups of bits to change together.

manuscripts.short_title: A superquadratic separation between sensitivity and block sensitivity
manuscripts.title: A superquadratic separation between sensitivity and block sensitivity

families.title: The complexity of Weisfeiler–Leman refinement
families.description: Proves unconditional n^Ω(k) deterministic time lower bounds for joint and separate k-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence, for sufficiently large fixed k in the specified sequential adjacency-matrix models. With dimension as input, joint equivalence is EXPTIME-complete even on subcubic graphs; deciding whether refinement identifies a graph is also EXPTIME-complete.

families.title: Generalized star height at most three
families.description: Every regular language over a finite alphabet has a generalized regular expression with at most three nested Kleene stars, allowing union, concatenation and complement over the same alphabet. This establishes an absolute bound independent of automaton size, resolving the uniform-boundedness version of the generalized star-height problem.

families.title: Sharp homogeneous depth-five complexity of matrix products
families.description: Over every characteristic-zero field, the (1,1) entry of a product of n independent n×n variable matrices requires n^Θ(√n) gates in homogeneous depth-five sum–product circuits. This sharp bound allows shared gates and bottom linear forms involving all variables.

manuscripts.short_title: Homogeneous depth-five lower bounds for iterated matrix multiplication
manuscripts.title: Homogeneous depth-five lower bounds for iterated matrix multiplication

families.title: The quasilinear PCP-for-PPAD conjecture
families.description: Resolves the quasilinear PCP-for-PPAD conjecture. An End-of-Line instance of length N reduces to numerical circuit constraints of total length N(logN)^O(1) such that any polynomially encoded rational assignment satisfying all but a fixed fraction to fixed accuracy yields an endpoint solution. Such assignments always exist, giving robust local verification with only quasilinear size overhead.

manuscripts.short_title: The PCP-for-PPAD conjecture: a quasilinear reduction
manuscripts.title: The PCP-for-PPAD conjecture: a quasilinear reduction

families.title: One-tape time simulation in two-fifths-power space
families.description: Determines the halting and finite-control outcome of a fixed deterministic one-writable-tape machine up to time T using O(T^2/5log^C(T+2)) space, improving the square-root exponent. Heads move at most one cell per step; finitely many read-only input heads are allowed. Initial contents are independent of T, and contents and input symbols have poly log arithmic-space access. Simulation time is unrestricted.

manuscripts.short_title: Simulating One-Tape Time in Two-Fifths-Power Space
manuscripts.title: Simulating One-Tape Time in Two-Fifths-Power Space

families.title: Subset Sum in O(2^0.49n) time
families.description: Gives a uniform randomized classical algorithm for worst-case Subset Sum in ordinary O(2^0.49n) word-RAM time on polynomial-bit inputs, where n counts the integers. The time bound holds on every execution and success probability is at least 2/3 on every input. Inputs may repeat positive integers; words have O(n+b) bits for maximum input bit length b.

manuscripts.short_title: A Low-Space Algorithm for Worst-Case Subset Sum
manuscripts.title: A Low-Space Algorithm for Worst-Case Subset Sum

families.title: Subpolynomial queries for log-concave sampling
families.description: For C^2 potentials with a supplied minimizer and I^2V2I, proves that sampling within total variation 1/10 requires only C_d^ exact value-and-gradient queries for every fixed >0. The bound holds on every run, with unrestricted computation between queries. A logarithmic lower bound also holds, so the optimal power-law exponent in this oracle model is zero.

manuscripts.short_title: Subpolynomial query complexity for well-conditioned log-concave sampling
manuscripts.title: Subpolynomial query complexity for well-conditioned log-concave sampling

families.title: Memory–sample lower bounds for noiseless Gaussian regression
families.description: For fixed A>0, a one-pass learner with Ad^2 persistent bits needs Ω_A(dlog(1/ε)) noiseless Gaussian samples to recover a unit vector to angular error 0<ε≤1/10 with probability 2/3, uniformly in accuracy for large d. Computation and randomized updates are unrestricted, but output uses only the terminal state, stopping index and fresh randomness.

families.title: The existential theory of the reals and existential–universal sentences in the counting hierarchy
families.description: Proves that the existential theory of the reals lies in the counting hierarchy. More generally, truth of existential–universal real sentences can be decided at one fixed level of that hierarchy, even when their integer polynomials are specified by arithmetic circuits.

manuscripts.short_title: Existential–universal real sentences in the counting hierarchy
manuscripts.title: Existential–universal real sentences in the counting hierarchy

families.title: Deterministic polynomial factorization over prime fields
families.description: Gives a uniform deterministic algorithm that completely factors every nonzero dense degree-n polynomial over a prime field F_p, including multiplicities, in bit complexity polynomial in (n+1)logp. The prime is supplied in binary. No randomness, integer-factorization or primitive-root oracle, or GRH assumption is required.

manuscripts.short_title: Deterministic Polynomial Factorization over Prime Fields
manuscripts.title: Deterministic Polynomial Factorization over Prime Fields

families.title: Uniform limit-cycle bounds in Hilbert's sixteenth problem
families.description: Resolves the uniform boundedness assertion in Hilbert's sixteenth problem: the number of isolated periodic orbits of a real planar polynomial vector field is bounded by a finite constant depending only on its degree. For classical quintic Liénard systems, the exact maximum is two limit cycles.

families.title: Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem
families.description: Resolves the probability-preserving form of Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem within smooth dynamics. A smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphism of the standard-volume three-torus has simple Lebesgue spectrum on its entire complex mean-zero L^2 space: the bilateral iterates of one real observable form an orthonormal basis of that space.

manuscripts.short_title: A smooth three-torus diffeomorphism with simple Lebesgue spectrum
manuscripts.title: A smooth three-torus diffeomorphism with simple Lebesgue spectrum

families.title: Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem
families.description: Proves that every invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation is mixing of all finite orders, resolving Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for a single transformation. Correlations among any finite collection of measurable sets converge to the product of their measures whenever all pairwise time separations diverge.

manuscripts.short_title: Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation
manuscripts.title: Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation

families.title: Sinai's positive-entropy conjecture for the standard map
families.description: Proves that the standard sine map on the two-dimensional torus has positive metric entropy with respect to area for every sufficiently large positive parameter. This establishes Sinai's positive-parameter-measure conjecture for the original family, with the stronger conclusion of a full parameter tail.

manuscripts.short_title: Positive Metric Entropy for the Standard Map at Large Parameters
manuscripts.title: Positive Metric Entropy for the Standard Map at Large Parameters

families.title: The near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture
families.description: Resolves the near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture for smooth strictly convex planar billiards of positive curvature. Such a billiard is an ellipse whenever a full grazing annulus is continuously foliated by individually invariant essential curves. A continuous physical collar of smooth closed convex caustics also suffices.

families.title: The dimension formula for self-similar measures on the line
families.description: For every self-similar measure on the line generated by finitely many contracting similarities, proves _Hμ=\1,h_RW/χ\, where h_RW is the entropy rate of random composed maps and χ the average logarithmic contraction. This resolves the entropy-rate dimension conjecture without a separation assumption, allowing exact overlaps and unequal contraction ratios.

manuscripts.short_title: The entropy-rate dimension formula for self-similar measures on the line
manuscripts.title: The entropy-rate dimension formula for self-similar measures on the line

families.title: Permanence for weakly reversible reaction networks
families.description: Proves the permanence conjecture for every finite weakly reversible mass-action system with fixed positive rate constants. Every positive stoichiometric compatibility class, even an unbounded one, has a common compact convex forward-invariant absorbing set. All positive trajectories in that class therefore eventually share positive lower and finite upper concentration bounds.

manuscripts.short_title: Uniform Permanence in Weakly Reversible Mass-Action Systems
manuscripts.title: Uniform Permanence in Weakly Reversible Mass-Action Systems

manuscripts.short_title: Boundedness and persistence of weakly reversible mass-action systems
manuscripts.title: Boundedness and persistence of weakly reversible mass-action systems

families.title: Weak mixing of irrational triangular billiards
families.description: Proves that the billiard flow in every nondegenerate Euclidean triangle with at least one angle irrational relative to π is weakly mixing for normalized area times uniform direction. This strengthens ergodicity on the entire irrational-angle class, with no genericity or Diophantine restrictions.

manuscripts.short_title: Weak mixing of triangular billiards with an irrational angle
manuscripts.title: Weak mixing of triangular billiards with an irrational angle

manuscripts.short_title: Ergodicity of triangular billiards with an irrational angle
manuscripts.title: Ergodicity of triangular billiards with an irrational angle

families.title: A C^1 counterexample to Shub’s entropy conjecture
families.description: Constructs a noninvertible C^1 self-map of a compact smooth manifold with zero topo log ical entropy but eigenvalue 2 on second homo log y. This disproves the homo log ical entropy lower bound for general C^1 self-maps: homo log ical growth need not force positive orbit complexity.

manuscripts.short_title: A C1 Counterexample to the Entropy Conjecture
manuscripts.title: A C1 Counterexample to the Entropy Conjecture

families.title: Zero entropy does not guarantee a smooth positive-volume model
families.description: Constructs a zero-entropy ergodic invertible transformation of a standard nonatomic probability space that is not measurably conjugate to any C^∞ diffeomorphism preserving a strictly positive smooth probability density on a compact finite-dimensional manifold. One example rules out every finite dimension.

manuscripts.short_title: A zero-entropy system without a smooth positive-volume model
manuscripts.title: A zero-entropy system without a smooth positive-volume model

families.title: Arithmetic classification of Bernoulli convolutions
families.description: Classifies singular and absolutely continuous unbiased Bernoulli convolutions for every λ(0,1) by an infinite, one-sided approximation condition using explicit finite sets of algebraic units. It also proves singularity at reciprocals of every quartic Salem number in (1,2), giving examples beyond reciprocal Pisot parameters.

manuscripts.short_title: Arithmetic classification and non-Pisot singularity for Bernoulli convolutions
manuscripts.title: Arithmetic classification and non-Pisot singularity for Bernoulli convolutions

families.title: Pointwise multiple ergodic averages for mixing transformations
families.description: Proves almost-everywhere convergence of consecutive multiple ergodic averages of every finite length for invertible mixing probability-preserving transformations. For each fixed tuple of bounded functions, the limit is the product of their integrals, along all positive averaging lengths. No mixing rate or standardness assumption on the probability space is required.

manuscripts.short_title: Pointwise Multiple Ergodic Averages for Mixing Transformations
manuscripts.title: Pointwise Multiple Ergodic Averages for Mixing Transformations

manuscripts.short_title: Pointwise convergence of fourfold ergodic averages for mixing transformations
manuscripts.title: Pointwise convergence of fourfold ergodic averages for mixing transformations

manuscripts.short_title: Triple ergodic averages with distinct integer slopes
manuscripts.title: Triple ergodic averages with distinct integer slopes

manuscripts.short_title: Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations
manuscripts.title: Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations

families.title: A counterexample to periodic tiling in dimension three
families.description: Constructs a finite translational tile in Z^3 that tiles space but admits no fully periodic tiling, disproving the periodic tiling conjecture in the smallest possible lattice dimension. Its unit-cube thickening gives the same counterexample in R^3, even with arbitrary real translation vectors.

manuscripts.short_title: A translational tile with no fully periodic tiling in dimension three
manuscripts.title: A translational tile with no fully periodic tiling in dimension three

families.title: Borsuk's conjecture fails in dimension nine
families.description: Constructs a compact subset of R^9 that cannot be covered by ten sets of strictly smaller diameter, disproving Borsuk's covering assertion already in dimension nine. The example consists of rank-one orthogonal projectors onto lines in R^4, with the Frobenius metric.

manuscripts.short_title: A nine-dimensional counterexample to Borsuk's covering assertion
manuscripts.title: A nine-dimensional counterexample to Borsuk's covering assertion

families.title: Counterexamples to the Hadwiger and Colin de Verdière conjectures
families.description: Disproves Hadwiger's conjecture even for fractional coloring: arbitrarily large finite simple graphs with independence number at most two satisfy χ_f(G)>h(G), where h(G) is the largest clique-minor order. Also disproves the fractional Colin de Verdière chromatic bound χ_f(G)≤μ(G)+1. In the positive direction, every finite nonempty graph satisfies χ_list(G)≤C h(G) for a universal constant C.

families.title: The Euclidean plane cannot be colored with five colors
families.description: Proves that every five-coloring of the Euclidean plane has a monochromatic pair at distance one, with no restriction on the color classes. This advances the Hadwiger–Nelson problem: together with the classical seven-coloring, only six and seven remain possible chromatic numbers of the plane.

manuscripts.short_title: The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable
manuscripts.title: The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable

families.title: Erdos's reciprocal-sum conjecture and quasipolynomial Szemerédi bounds
families.description: Proves Erdos's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length. Quantitatively, for each fixed k≥3, every subset of \1,,N\ with no nonconstant k-term progression has size at most C_kN[-c_k(logN)^_k], with positive constants depending only on k.

families.title: Superexponential van der Waerden numbers
families.description: Resolves Erdos's superexponential-growth question for van der Waerden numbers. If W_r(k) is the least interval length forcing a monochromatic k-term progression in every r-coloring, then W_r(k)>k^ck log _2 r for an absolute c>0, all r≥2 and sufficiently large k, uniformly in r. In particular, W_r(k)^1/k∞ for each fixed r.

manuscripts.short_title: Quantitative Superexponential Bounds for van der Waerden Numbers
manuscripts.title: Quantitative Superexponential Bounds for van der Waerden Numbers

families.title: Counterexamples to Sidorenko's conjecture and the forcing conjecture
families.description: Disproves Sidorenko's conjecture with a connected bipartite pattern on 35 vertices and 66 edges that occurs less frequently than in a random graph of the same edge density. The same pattern disproves the forcing conjecture of Skokan and Thoma: matching its density and the edge density of a constant graphon need not force quasirandomness.

families.title: Counterexamples to Ryser's covering and Gyárfás's tree-cover conjectures
families.description: Disproves Ryser's covering conjecture by constructing intersecting (q+1)-partite, (q+1)-uniform hypergraphs with covering number q+1, rather than the predicted bound q, for every sufficiently large prime q. A separate construction over extension fields also disproves Gyárfás's monochromatic tree-cover conjecture.

families.title: Hindman's finite sums and products conjecture
families.description: Proves Hindman's finite sums and products conjecture: every finite coloring of the positive integers contains sets of any prescribed finite size whose nonempty subset sums and nonempty subset products all have one common color.

manuscripts.short_title: Monochromatic finite sums and products in the positive integers
manuscripts.title: Monochromatic finite sums and products in the positive integers

families.title: Exact crossing numbers of complete and complete bipartite graphs
families.description: Resolves the Harary–Hill conjecture and Turán's brickyard problem in the Zarankiewicz formulation, determining the crossing numbers of every complete and complete bipartite graph. The result proves the optimality of the classical drawings among all plane drawings with continuous edge arcs.

families.title: The higher-dimensional Erdos distinct-distances conjecture
families.description: For every fixed d≥3, any n≥2 distinct points in R^d determine at least c_dn^2/d distinct distances, with c_d>0 depending only on dimension. This matches the integer-grid order and resolves the higher-dimensional Erdos distinct-distances conjecture with a constant-factor bound.

families.title: Pinned distances and a power saving for planar unit distances
families.description: Proves the weak pinned Erdos distance conjecture: for every fixed >0, all but o(n) points of any n-point planar set determine at least n^1- distinct nonzero distances. A complementary theorem bounds the number of unit-distance pairs by O(n^4/3-δ) for an absolute δ>0.

families.title: Combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
families.description: Resolves the full combinatorial invariance conjecture: isomorphic Bruhat intervals in arbitrary Coxeter systems have identical equal-parameter Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials. Thus the abstract order of the interval determines the polynomial, even across different Coxeter systems.

families.title: The Shareshian–Wachs e-positivity conjecture
families.description: Resolves the elementary-positivity part of the Shareshian–Wachs conjecture: the chromatic quasisymmetric function of every natural unit interval graph has elementary-basis coefficients in N[q]. The coefficients count explicitly described permutations, giving a combinatorial explanation of positivity.

manuscripts.short_title: Elementary positivity of chromatic quasisymmetric functions
manuscripts.title: Elementary positivity of chromatic quasisymmetric functions

families.title: Sharp logarithmic exponents for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers
families.description: For every fixed integer s≥5, proves r(s,t)=t^s-1/(logt)^s-2+o(1) as t∞, determining the logarithmic exponent and matching the classical upper bound at that scale. Here r(s,t) is the least number of vertices forcing an s-clique or a t-vertex independent set.

families.title: The hypercube Ramsey conjecture
families.description: Resolves the Burr–Erdos hypercube Ramsey conjecture: the two-color Ramsey number of the n-dimensional cube is Θ(2^n). Thus every red-blue coloring of a complete graph on a universal constant times the cube's number of vertices contains a monochromatic copy of the cube.

manuscripts.short_title: The hypercube Ramsey number has linear order
manuscripts.title: The hypercube Ramsey number has linear order

families.title: Classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations
families.description: Classifies finite point configurations that occur monochromatically, at their original scale, in every finite coloring of sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space. The characterization is an algebraic condition over the coordinate field. It also disproves the Leader–Russell–Walters conjecture that every such configuration is a subset of a finite transitive set.

manuscripts.short_title: A classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations
manuscripts.title: A classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations

families.title: Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture
families.description: Proves Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture: every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many vertices at directed distance exactly two as at directed distance one. Oriented graphs may be arbitrary apart from the exclusion of loops and oppositely directed edge pairs.

manuscripts.short_title: A proof of Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture
manuscripts.title: A proof of Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture

families.title: Deterministic construction of strong thin spanning trees
families.description: Resolves the strong thin-tree conjecture constructively. Every finite loopless k-edge-connected multigraph on at least two vertices has a spanning tree containing at most a universal C/k fraction of the edges of every cut. Such a tree can be found deterministically in polynomial time, even with binary-encoded parallel-edge multiplicities.

families.title: Talagrand's conjectures and graph decompositions at expectation thresholds
families.description: Proves that integral and fractional expectation thresholds differ by at most a universal factor, and resolves Talagrand's discrete-convexity conjecture. An application proves the Ascoli–He–Park–Talagrand graph-decomposition conjecture: every graph's edges split into a universally bounded number of fixed pieces, each with containment threshold at most a universal constant times the original graph's integral expectation threshold. The pieces' embeddings need not agree on shared vertices.

manuscripts.short_title: Graph Decompositions at the Integral Expectation Threshold
manuscripts.title: Graph Decompositions at the Integral Expectation Threshold

families.title: The second Kahn–Kalai conjecture
families.description: Proves the second Kahn–Kalai conjecture: for every finite simple graph H with h≥1 edges and at most n vertices, its appearance threshold in G(n,p) is at most C p_E(n,H)(1+log_2 h), with universal C. Here p_E is the least density at which every subgraph of H has expected copy count at least 1/2.

families.title: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension
families.description: Constructs arbitrarily large finite d-dimensional simplicial complexes, for every d≥3, with uniformly bounded vertex degrees and uniform F_2 coboundary expansion in every degree below d. Together with the known graph and two-dimensional cases, this establishes the existence of such expanders in every positive dimension.

manuscripts.short_title: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension
manuscripts.title: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension

families.title: Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree
families.description: For every fixed d≥3, constructs a simple d-regular nonbipartite Ramanujan graph on every sufficiently large even number n of vertices, with every nonconstant adjacency eigenvalue strictly between -2√d-1 and 2√d-1. A deterministic algorithm outputs the full adjacency list in polynomial bit time, with exponent depending on d.

manuscripts.short_title: Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree
manuscripts.title: Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree

families.title: The circulant Hadamard conjecture
families.description: Proves that real circulant Hadamard matrices exist exactly in orders 1 and 4, resolving the circulant Hadamard conjecture. Together with classical Barker-sequence results, this shows that binary sequences whose nontrivial aperiodic autocorrelations have magnitude at most 1 exist at lengths n>1 exactly when n\2,3,4,5,7,11,13\.

families.title: Barnette's Hamiltonian-cycle conjecture
families.description: Proves that every finite simple cubic bipartite planar 3-vertex-connected graph has a Hamiltonian cycle, resolving Barnette's conjecture. Equivalently, every three-edge path in a finite simple cubic 3-vertex-connected bipartite Pfaffian graph lies in a Hamiltonian cycle.

manuscripts.short_title: Paired states and Hamiltonian cycles in cubic bipartite planar graphs
manuscripts.title: Paired states and Hamiltonian cycles in cubic bipartite planar graphs

families.title: The Erdos–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture
families.description: Proves that the edges of every finite simple undirected graph on n vertices can be partitioned into at most Cn simple cycles and single edges, for an absolute constant C. This resolves the Erdos–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture, bounding the number of pieces linearly even for dense graphs.

manuscripts.short_title: A linear cycle-and-edge decomposition of every graph
manuscripts.title: A linear cycle-and-edge decomposition of every graph

families.title: Power savings for polynomial-difference-free sets
families.description: For every fixed intersective integer polynomial h of degree k≥2 with positive leading coefficient, proves that a subset of \1,,N\ avoiding nonzero values h(1),h(2), as differences has size O_h(N^1-c_k), with c_k>0 depending only on degree. Here intersective means having a root modulo every modulus. For prime arguments, a power saving also holds when h has a unit root modulo every modulus, with exponent allowed to depend on h.

manuscripts.short_title: A power saving for intersective polynomial differences with an exponent depending only on the degree
manuscripts.title: A power saving for intersective polynomial differences with an exponent depending only on the degree

manuscripts.short_title: A Power Saving for Polynomial Differences at Prime Arguments
manuscripts.title: A Power Saving for Polynomial Differences at Prime Arguments

manuscripts.short_title: A power saving for square-difference-free sets
manuscripts.title: A power saving for square-difference-free sets

families.title: Power savings for planar halving lines and k-sets
families.description: Improves the planar halving-line bound to O(n^4/3-) for sets with no three collinear and an absolute >0. More generally, an n-point set with no three collinear has O(n(k+1)^1/3-_0) strictly separable k-subsets for 1≤k≤n/2, with an absolute _0>0. The constants and positive exponents are nonquantitative.

manuscripts.short_title: A power saving for planar halving lines
manuscripts.title: A power saving for planar halving lines

families.title: Coloring and independence in graphs with forbidden subgraphs
families.description: Proves the Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov coloring conjecture in correspondence-coloring form: graphs avoiding any fixed subgraph F need O_F(Δ/logΔ) colors when their maximum degree Δ is sufficiently large. Also proves the Ajtai–Erdos–Komlós–Szemerédi independence conjecture: for fixed r≥4, every n-vertex K_r-free graph of average degree d≥2 has an independent set of size Ω_r(n log d/d).

manuscripts.short_title: Correspondence coloring graphs with a forbidden clique
manuscripts.title: Correspondence coloring graphs with a forbidden clique

manuscripts.short_title: A logarithmic independence bound for clique-free graphs
manuscripts.title: A logarithmic independence bound for clique-free graphs

families.title: Counterexamples to infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering
families.description: Disproves the unrestricted infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering conjectures in ZFC, using two self-dual partitional matroids on a countably infinite ground set. The same examples answer Joó’s partitional-matroid question negatively. They are neither finitary nor cofinitary, so Nash-Williams’ original finitary conjecture remains outside the result.

manuscripts.short_title: A Counterexample to the Infinite Matroid Packing/Covering Conjecture
manuscripts.title: A Counterexample to the Infinite Matroid Packing/Covering Conjecture

families.title: The Friedgut–Kalai graph and hypergraph threshold conjectures
families.description: Proves the Friedgut–Kalai threshold-width conjectures for graphs and fixed-uniformity hypergraphs. For fixed 0<<1/2, every nontrivial increasing relabeling-invariant property crosses from probability to 1- within width O((logn)^-2) for graphs and O_r((logn)^-r/(r-1)) for r-uniform hypergraphs, r≥3. The hypergraph influence bound also applies to nonmonotone properties.

manuscripts.short_title: A uniform influence bound for hypergraph properties
manuscripts.title: A uniform influence bound for hypergraph properties

manuscripts.short_title: A Sharp Threshold Bound for Monotone Graph Properties
manuscripts.title: A Sharp Threshold Bound for Monotone Graph Properties

families.title: Snaky in 21 Maker moves
families.description: Settles the Snaky achievement problem: Maker can force the six-cell Snaky shape within 21 of its own moves on the initially empty infinite square board. Maker moves first, each player claims one free cell per turn, and translations, rotations and reflections count as wins.

families.title: The sharp constant in random triangle removal
families.description: Starting from the complete graph on n vertices, repeatedly delete a uniformly chosen remaining triangle. The terminal edge count is asymptotic to n^3/2/(2√2), with mean-square convergence after normalization by n^3/2. This proves the triangle case of the Joos–Kühn sharp-constant conjecture.

manuscripts.short_title: The sharp terminal leave in random triangle removal
manuscripts.title: The sharp terminal leave in random triangle removal

families.title: Exact cycle–clique Ramsey numbers
families.description: Proves the Erdos–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture: R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1 for every m≥n≥3, except R(C_3,K_3)=6. This is the exact threshold forcing a red m-cycle or a blue n-clique in every red–blue coloring of a complete graph.

families.title: Polynomial removal fails for ordered binary matrices
families.description: Disproves polynomial ordered binary matrix removal with one fixed 66×66 zero–one pattern. Matrices can require many binary-entry changes to become pattern-free while their copy density is smaller than every proposed polynomial bound in that distance. Copies preserve row and column orders and match both zeros and ones.

families.title: A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle problem
families.description: For every sufficiently large n, constructs n points in the unit square such that every triangle has area at least n^-2+c for one absolute c>0. This disproves the conjectured almost-n^-2 upper bound in Heilbronn's triangle problem, which asks how large the smallest determined triangle can be.

families.title: A counterexample to the Gopalan–Servedio conjecture
families.description: Disproves the proposed square-root bound relating a Boolean function's linear Fourier coefficients to its polynomial degree. For every C>0, there is a sign-valued Boolean function f with _if(\i\)>C√(f). Thus its total signed correlation with individual input bits can exceed the proposed bound by an arbitrary factor.

families.title: Serre's intersection-multiplicity conjecture
families.description: Proves strict positivity of Serre's intersection multiplicity χ^R(M,N) for nonzero finitely generated modules over any regular local ring, provided M⊗_R N has finite length and M+N=R. This resolves the positivity conjecture, including ramified mixed characteristic.

families.title: Lech's multiplicity conjecture
families.description: Proves e(R)≤e(S) for every flat local homomorphism of nonzero Noetherian local rings, where e is Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity. This resolves Lech's conjecture in every dimension and characteristic.

families.title: A counterexample to the small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture
families.description: Constructs a three-dimensional complete Noetherian normal local domain over C with no nonzero finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay module. A three-dimensional local domain essentially of finite type over C has the same property, disproving the domain form of the small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture.

families.title: A counterexample to Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture
families.description: Constructs a finitely presented torsion-free group G whose group algebra F_2[G] has nonzero zero divisors, disproving Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture. The group has a finite two-dimensional classifying space.

families.title: Nonsofic groups and group-ring counterexamples
families.description: Constructs a finitely presented torsion-free nonsofic group whose group algebra over F_2 is not directly finite, disproving Kaplansky's conjecture even without torsion. Companion examples give injective nonsurjective cellular automata on all configurations, refuting Gottschalk's surjunctivity conjecture. Another counterexample is an integral group-ring matrix, invertible over the rational group ring, with Fuglede–Kadison determinant strictly between zero and one, disproving the unrestricted Determinant Conjecture.

families.title: A counterexample to the little finitistic-dimension conjecture
families.description: Constructs a finite-dimensional complex algebra whose finite-dimensional modules have unbounded finite projective dimensions. This disproves the little finitistic-dimension conjecture.

families.title: Counterexamples to conjectures of Auslander–Reiten, Tachikawa, and Nakayama
families.description: Constructs finite-dimensional algebras over a characteristic-two rational-function field that disprove the Auslander–Reiten and Gorenstein-projective conjectures, and Tachikawa's second conjecture. An associated endomorphism algebra also disproves the classical, generalized and strong Nakayama conjectures, the Auslander–Gorenstein conjecture, and the Wakamatsu tilting conjecture. The counterexamples persist under every extension of the base field.

families.title: Eisenbud–Green–Harris and lex-plus-powers in characteristic zero
families.description: Proves the Eisenbud–Green–Harris and lex-plus-powers conjectures over every characteristic-zero field. Any homogeneous ideal containing a regular sequence, of arbitrary length and degrees at least two, admits a lex-plus-powers ideal with the same Hilbert function and no smaller graded Betti numbers.

families.title: A counterexample to Kurosh's division-ring problem
families.description: Constructs a countable characteristic-zero division ring that is algebraic over its center and generated by two elements over that center, but has infinite dimension over it. This answers Kurosh's division-ring problem on local finiteness negatively.

families.title: The blockwise Alperin weight conjecture
families.description: Proves the numerical blockwise Alperin weight conjecture for every prime and every finite group: the number of irreducible Brauer characters in a block equals the number of conjugacy classes of its weights.

families.title: Donovan's conjecture over fields and discrete valuation rings
families.description: Proves Donovan's conjecture: over each fixed algebraically closed field of characteristic p, blocks of finite groups with bounded defect-group order have only finitely many Morita-equivalence classes, for every prime p. Also proves the integral form over each fixed complete mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring with algebraically closed residue field.

families.title: Tensor saturation for even spin groups
families.description: Proves saturation factor one for Spin(2n), n≥2: for three dominant integral weights whose sum lies in the root lattice, an invariant at any common positive integral dilation already gives an invariant at the original weights. This resolves the type-D part of the simply-laced saturation conjecture.

families.title: Saxl's conjecture and universal tensor squares
families.description: Proves Saxl's conjecture: the tensor square of every staircase representation contains every irreducible complex representation of the corresponding symmetric group. More generally, every S_n with n\2,4,9\ has an irreducible representation whose tensor square contains all irreducibles.

families.title: Finite lattice representation: counterexamples and undecidability
families.description: Some finite lattices are not congruence lattices of any finite algebra, answering the finite lattice representation problem negatively. Moreover, no algorithm decides whether a finite lattice has such a representation, or whether it is a full subgroup interval of a finite group.

families.title: The ℓ^1-Bass and complex Bass trace conjectures
families.description: Proves the ℓ^1-Bass conjecture for every discrete group: Hattori–Stallings traces of idempotent matrices over ℓ^1(G) are supported on finitely many finite-order conjugacy classes. The algebraic companion proves the integral Bass trace conjecture and Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture for torsion-free groups over every commutative unital characteristic-zero domain.

families.title: The finite Benson–Etingof–Ostrik conjecture
families.description: Proves that every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0 admits a k-linear exact faithful strong symmetric monoidal fiber functor to a higher Verlinde category Ver_p^n. The level may depend on the category, and the theorem includes characteristic two, resolving the finite case of the Benson–Etingof–Ostrik conjecture.

families.title: Integral counterexamples to Gersten’s conjecture
families.description: Disproves unrestricted integral Gersten injectivity in degrees 3 and 5. Two explicit two-dimensional ramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic (0,5) have nonzero integral K-theory classes that vanish over their fraction fields.

families.title: Foulkes’ conjecture for sixth powers and quadratic stabilization
families.description: Proves the sixth case of Foulkes’ conjecture: Sym^6(Sym^bV) embeds equivariantly in Sym^b(Sym^6V) for every b≥6 and finite-dimensional complex V. More generally, the canonical multiplication map Sym^b(Sym^aV)Sym^a(Sym^bV) is surjective for a≥2 and b≥a(a-1), giving dimension-independent quadratic stabilization.

families.title: Geometry, diffusion, and spectra of random planar maps
families.description: Critical Fortuin–Kasteleyn planar maps converge to Liouville quantum gravity spheres for 0<q≤4 and to the Brownian continuum random tree for q>4, establishing the surface-to-tree geometric transition. For FK–Ising and spanning-tree-weighted maps, stationary random walks converge to Liouville Brownian motion on the limiting sphere. The FK–Ising spectral result also gives convergence of eigenvalues and heat traces, using the stated Brownian/LQG inputs.

families.title: No bigeodesics and smooth limit shapes in planar first-passage percolation
families.description: Proves that planar first-passage percolation has no doubly infinite geodesic for iid nonnegative nonatomic edge weights when the minimum of four weights has finite second moment. For exponential weights, the limit shape is strictly convex with C^1 boundary. Differentiability also holds for every Gamma law with positive shape and rate.

families.title: No infinite critical clusters on quasi-transitive graphs
families.description: Resolves the Benjamini–Schramm criticality conjecture for bond percolation on every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph with p_c<1: at the critical probability, there is almost surely no infinite cluster. The family also establishes this conclusion for both nearest-neighbor bond and site percolation on Z^3.

families.title: The Benjamini–Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture
families.description: Proves p_c<p_u for Bernoulli bond percolation on every infinite connected locally finite nonamenable quasi-transitive graph, resolving the Benjamini–Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture. Thus there is a nonempty range of probabilities with infinitely many infinite clusters. A stronger operator bound also establishes the critical triangle condition.
